ozone.short: A gas (O₃) that forms near the ground when sunlight acts on traffic and industry fumes. It peaks on hot, sunny afternoons and irritates the airways.

particulate-matter.short: Tiny solid or liquid specks floating in the air, from traffic, wood fires, industry and wildfires. The smaller they are, the deeper into the lungs they can go.

pm25.short: Particulate matter with specks 2.5 micrometres across or smaller, far thinner than a hair. Measured in µg·m⁻³ (micrograms in each cubic metre of air).

no2.short: A brownish gas made when fuel burns at high heat, mostly from diesel traffic. It is high near busy roads and irritates the airways.

air-quality-index.short: A single number or colour that turns the measured pollutant levels into a health warning. Higher is worse. Scales and cut-offs differ between countries.

inhaled-dose.short: How much of a pollutant you breathe in: its concentration in the air multiplied by how much air you breathe (minute ventilation) and for how long.

zeitgeber.short: German for time-giver: a cue that sets the body clock, mainly light, but also meal times, exercise and social routine.

phase-shift.short: Moving the body clock earlier (an advance) or later (a delay). After flying east the clock must advance, after flying west it must delay.

jet-lag.short: The clash between your body clock and local time after crossing three or more time zones. It brings poor sleep, tiredness and weaker performance until the clock catches up.

melatonin.short: A hormone the brain releases in the evening in dim light. Taken as a pill at the right time it can move the body clock, but at the wrong time it moves it the wrong way.

core-temp-minimum.short: The low point of the daily body-temperature curve, usually in the last hours of sleep. It marks where the body clock is, and tells you when light helps or hurts.

travel-fatigue.short: Tiredness and low mood from any long journey (a bus, a car, a flight), in any direction. It can build up over a season of trips, and it needs no time-zone change.
